title: Antony goes into the desert
hookLine: a young Egyptian hears 'go and sell that thou hast' read in church, and does it, and in time walks into the desert

lines: AN INHERITANCE AND A LITTLE SISTER.
WHAT WOULD THAT LOOK LIKE NOW?
HE WALKS IN AT THAT MOMENT.
cards: A young man in an Egyptian village has just buried his parents. He's inherited good farmland, and he's responsible for his little sister.

Walking to church, he's turning something over: the apostles left everything to follow Jesus, and in the book of Acts, believers sold their land and laid the money at the apostles' feet. What would that look like now?
He walks in, and at that moment the Gospel being read is the one about a rich young man. His name is Antony. His Life was written by Athanasius, bishop of Alexandria.

teach.h: GO AND SELL THAT THOU HAST.
teach.b: Here's the verse he heard, from Matthew, in the King James Bible: "If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me."
Athanasius says Antony felt the words had been read for him. In the Gospel, the rich young man goes away sorrowful. Antony goes out and does it.
He gives his family's land to the people of his village, sells the rest, and gives the money to the poor, keeping a little back for his sister.

teach.h: TAKE NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW.
teach.b: Then he walks into church again and hears another line: "Take therefore no thought for the morrow."
So he gives away what he'd kept, places his sister with a community of faithful women, and begins a life of prayer and work. He doesn't vanish into the sand that afternoon.

teach.h: THE VILLAGE EDGE, THE TOMBS, THE DESERT.
teach.b: He starts at the edge of his village, learning from an old man who lives that way, moves out to the tombs, and only later crosses into the desert, farther and farther in.
Athanasius says he wrote the Life because monks in other places asked what Antony was like.

teach.h: A VOCATION, OR A MATTER OF THE HEART?
teach.b: Catholic and Orthodox churches honor Antony as a father of monastic life, and there the call to sell everything is a real vocation some are given.

Other Christians, among them some Protestants, read the verse as aimed at what holds a person's heart, and practice it through generosity rather than leaving home. Both readings take the verse seriously.
What lands is the speed. He heard. And he went.

how: Catholic and Orthodox churches honor Antony as a father of monasticism and keep his feast; monks and nuns take vows of poverty, while other Christians practice the same verse through giving and simple living.

o: a bishop of Alexandria who wrote the lives of the desert monks
the rich young man in Matthew who went away from Jesus sorrowful
an Egyptian who gave everything away and went into the desert

p: go and sell that thou hast
the verse he heard in church

s: Antony went straight into the deep desert the day he heard the verse
he began at the edge of his village, then the tombs, and only later the desert.
Antony kept a little back for his sister at first
then, hearing 'take no thought for the morrow', he gave that away too.
Athanasius says he wrote the Life because monks asked about Antony
monks in other places wanted to know what he was like.

games.q: you're Antony. you've just heard 'go and sell that thou hast' read in church, and you have land and a little sister. what do you do?
o: go away sorrowful, like the rich young man.
give away the land, sell the rest, keep a little for your sister.
wait a few years until your sister is grown.
games.why: he gives his land to the village and the money to the poor, keeping a little for his sister, until the next verse he hears.

practice: Walk in your mind through a closet, a shelf or a drawer, and find one thing you don't need that someone else could use, not the easiest junk but something with a little weight to it.
Decide where it would go; if you pray, offer it to God as you let it go, and if not, hold it in your mind and open your hand.

wordCard.voice: Antony. A young Egyptian who heard go and sell that thou hast, gave it away, and step by step walked into a life of prayer in the desert.

orig.note: Greek: monk. the word the Life uses for the monks who asked Athanasius what Antony was like.

carryVoice: Your line: he heard, and went. No waiting to feel ready. Day seven hundred sixty-five, done.
